text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.1% today, reversing four straight days of gains and closing near its lowest point in two weeks. The decline comes as Russian crude production has rebounded sharply—now back above 8.7 million barrels a day—pushing global oil markets into surplus (more supply than demand). With crude prices sliding toward $90 a barrel and refineries already running at 95% capacity, the outlook for refiner margins has tightened; more crude chasing the same demand means less profit per barrel processed.

The broader headwinds are compounding. Heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year, which typically signals strong seasonal demand—but it's also pricing out consumers and creating economic anxiety that could dampen fuel demand heading into winter. At the same time, rising shipping costs are making retailers cautious on holiday inventory, which could slow transportation fuel consumption precisely when refiners were counting on seasonal strength.
